hiring.requires_chilean_title_note: No current academic vacancy is published, so there is no open academic-post requirement on foreign degrees, revalidación, or nationality to quote. For clinical-specialty admission (not employment), UOH states: “El título obtenido de médico cirujano debe ser otorgado por una Universidad Chilena o una Universidad extranjera (revalidado en Chile).”

international.notes: The published Medicina curriculum lists Inglés 1–6 as separate modules, not medicine subjects delivered in English. UOH's Dirección de Internacionalización manages mobility for students, professors, researchers and staff; incoming exchange students may take a semester in undergraduate programmes where a mobility agreement exists.

profile_paragraphs: UOH’s medical education is housed in the Escuela de Salud, not a separate Faculty of Medicine. The University reports that it began forming its undergraduate schools, including Health, in 2017; Medicina’s first cohort also entered in 2017.
Medicina is based at Campus Rancagua. Its published programme is a 14-semester, in-person daytime degree, accredited by CNA for four years from 3 September 2025 to 3 September 2029.

Daniela Flores Meza is the current Director of the Escuela de Salud. The programme has designated clinical-cycle and internship coordinators, and names the Hospital Dr. Franco Ravera Zunino as a clinical-training partner under a Relación Asistencial Docente agreement.

For a rheumatologist, the linked regional hospital provides adult rheumatology care, and UOH’s Medicina Interna specialty includes a rheumatology rotation. UOH does not publish a standalone rheumatology specialty; its current specialty list includes Internal Medicine but not Rheumatology.

There were no open academic posts on 3 September 2026. A clinical route would require separate Chilean recognition: UOH’s 2026 specialty-admission rules require a foreign medical degree to be revalidated in Chile.
